reason: Hypothesis A directly addresses the limitation of low coercivity in prior FeCoNiPd/Pt alloys by proposing a specific, testable substitution (Mn) with a physically sound mechanism (antiferromagnetic coupling and lattice strain pinning domain walls), while staying within the high-entropy alloy constraints. Hypothesis B introduces a dual-phase microstructure and cites precise coercivity values (667 Oe) and transition temperatures without supporting evidence, which violates the 'no invented precise values' criterion and makes it less grounded.
